_README: THE one settings file (Chris 2026-11-03). Shared sections apply to every machine; 'machines' holds one block per outreach machine with IDENTICAL keys — a new machine is a copy of one block plus a template (Rulebook §5). Paths: {root} = Automations/, {master} = _shared/master/, {marketing} = Marketing/. Where everything lives: _shared/orchestrator/paths.py. The 'why' behind each number is in RULEBOOK.md (Appendix A).
_holidays_note: Federal Reserve schedule: a holiday on Saturday is not observed (Fed open the Friday before); a holiday on Sunday is observed Monday. 2026-07-04, 2027-06-19 and 2027-12-25 fall on Saturdays.

discovery._README: Discovery engine caps and order (Rulebook D; Stage 4 2026-10-31). Lower priority sweeps first. Re-sweep intervals reused from Machine 2.
discovery._om2_search_share_why: Chris 2026-11-06 (option 2): when a discover run serves both machines, OM-2 batches get this share of the run's searches

draft._README: Stage 7 (5_Draft/programfiles/draft.py): Email 1 drafts. Code fills the approved template verbatim (only greeting + org short name vary); Zapier creates each draft (clean links, real PDF); Gate 7 checks the raw attachment bytes. Minimums are floors to aim for, never a reason to lower a gate; max_per_night is the ceiling (Chris 2026-10-30: OM-1 10, OM-2 35). Per-machine minimum / ceiling / subject / template / attachment: machines.<OM>.

inputs._README: READ-ONLY inputs. Outside this folder: the do-not-contact register and the Head Start grantee list. seeds/ = legacy files from the old machines that build_master.py still reads to seed ~1,600 organizations (Chris 2026-11-03: never archive them or the nightly rebuild drops orgs). Machine ledgers (contacted / events) live in _shared/machines/. Phase ledgers are named in paths.py, not here.

OM-1._hard_bounces_note: PUBLIC COPY: notes trimmed; shape is {address: {org, sent, dsn, note}}.

zapier.never: update_draft on a Zapier-created draft - the native connector rebuilds the message, strips the attachment and re-wraps the hrefs. reply_parent_rule.detect: hidden = get_thread(threadId).messageCount - messages it lists - live drafts on the thread (the native connector omits drafts and trashed messages). hidden > 0 => assume a trashed draft is the newest message => the new draft will be COMPOSE-LINK-ONLY. Say so on the card and count it on the Draft writer: line. Never silently create an invisible draft without flagging it.
reply_parent_rule.normal_nights: Unaffected: a due follow-up's thread normally ends with Chris's sent mail (or a bounce/auto-reply), which is a visible parent. The risk case is a thread where Chris trashed a draft without sending and the machine drafts it again.
reply_parent_rule.rebuild: An edit/rebuild of a Zapier draft = trash the old draft, ASK CHRIS to delete it forever (or empty Trash), THEN create the replacement. If it cannot wait: create it, flag COMPOSE-LINK-ONLY on the card.
reply_parent_rule.rule: Create a Zapier reply ONLY when the newest message on the thread is a real message (sent mail, bounce, auto-reply, reply). Trashing an older draft does NOT clear the way; only Chris deleting it FOREVER (Trash > Delete forever, or Empty Trash) removes it from the thread. The machine cannot delete forever.
reply_parent_rule.subject_check: BEFORE creating a reply: read the thread with the native get_thread (MINIMAL) and take the newest listed message's subject. If it is not the thread's own subject (ignoring 'Re: ') - i.e. the newest message is a bounce, auto-reply or anything else - do NOT reply on that thread. Create the follow-up with draft_v2 as a NEW thread, subject 'Re: <the thread's subject>', same To/Cc, same body, signature, label; record new_thread on the card and in the ledger status (the recipient still sees a normal 'Re:' email; on Chris's side it is a separate conversation). Done for YWCA 2026-10-04: draft r3352886311815312191 on thread <id>.
reply_parent_rule.subject_inheritance: FOUND 2026-10-04 during the 36-draft rebuild: a Zapier reply also inherits the SUBJECT of the message it replies to. YWCA's E1 thread had the Cc hard-bounce as its newest message, so the reply was titled 'Delivery Status Notification (Failure)'. An auto-reply as newest message would give 'Automatic reply: …'. The 15 other Email 2 replies (parent = Email 1) read 'Question about PD/Training at …' with no Re:; the 8 Email 3 replies (parent = sent Email 2) read 'Re: …'.

night._README: Untimed night run, NEVER SENDS (Chris 2026-10-31: two tasks for safety). ONE start Sun–Thu ~8:41 PM MT: inbox read → label state (Rulebook L) → tomorrow's APPROVED SEND LIST (sendlist.py build; flagged = not approved) → review-hold DRAFTS → the LOOP {discover → qualify → people → draft Email 1} until every machine meets its nightly minimum or is supply-exhausted (or the pass ceiling) → the one report. No step deadlines, no waiting. The 07:00 ET send is the separate send task (_shared/orchestrator/run.py send), its own lock lane.
night._loop_steps_why: Chris 2026-11-08: the night starts on the shelf the Supply Run stocked — people and drafts first; discover/qualify only for a machine still under its minimum after that

loop._apollo_floor_why: people-step Apollo lookups stop when the cycle's remaining credits fall below this (Claude default 2026-10-31)
loop._max_passes_why: last-resort runaway guard (Chris 2026-10-31); hitting it is reported
loop._no_progress: a machine whose full pass adds 0 drafts, 0 new people-ready orgs and 0 newly qualified orgs is supply-exhausted for the night (Chris 2026-10-31)

night.pointer_prompt: Mount the vault: call get_device_info; if connectedFolders is empty, call device_request_folder_access for /Users/<you>/ClaudeVault once. If it is still unreachable, stop and say so. On the device shell run:  python3 "$HOME/mnt/ClaudeVault/3.Human Skills Training/Marketing/Automations/_shared/orchestrator/run.py" night   It prints your standing orders. Do exactly what they say, step by step, until they are complete. If it prints FAIL CLOSED, or the file is missing, stop and say so. Never do anything the orders did not print.

pending_rulings.question: Nightly Email 1 ceilings: OM-1 15 / OM-2 50 are in use as defaults — pending Chris's confirmation (Stage 7, 2026-10-31).

Address validity: Apollo's per-address validation needs approval on every call, so nightly runs treat validity as UNKNOWN → proceed, flagged (bounces guarded by the 3% breaker) — pending Chris: give that tool standing approval, or keep this default.

People Apollo cannot confirm (common at small orgs) proceed FLAGGED on the strength of the org's own live page (Machine 1's live-page exception) — pending Chris's confirmation of this exception to Rulebook H2.

people._README: Stage 6 (4_People/programfiles/people.py): find up to 4 people per org by ROLE (Rulebook G) and check every address (Rulebook H): live-page character match or the org's own auto-reply (H6), Apollo identity, validity (hold only on a definite invalid). Chris 2026-10-31. Role order per machine: machines.<OM>.role_rank.
people._domain_check_cap_why: Rulebook B4 patch 2 (Chris 2026-11-10): at most this many unknown domains are checked in Apollo per run (free people search). Adjust after the first runs.

apollo._zerobounce_interim_skip_why: Chris 2026-11-09: until his ZeroBounce account exists, an Apollo-found address that is Verified and on the org's own domain is used, flagged ⚠ ZeroBounce not run. Set false once the validator can run.
apollo.identity: apollo_people_match (name + org domain; email given) — confirms the person is real and still at the org; not in Apollo = proceed flagged (the live page is the evidence, Machine 1's live-page exception)
apollo.validity: apollo_email_validation_validate (ZeroBounce-class vendor) or the email_status Apollo returns for that exact address; hold ONLY on a definite invalid; catch-all/unknown proceed flagged

qualify._README: Stage 5 (3_Qualify/programfiles/qualify.py): fit from verified live-page quotes; routing + timing are computed in build_master.py (Rulebook C/E/F). Chris 2026-10-31.

send_task._README: Chris 2026-10-31: a separate weekday task fires ~06:52 America/New_York, waits in-session to 07:00 ET, sends only the approved list. Only this task gets automatic approval.

sender._README: Live sends happen ONLY in the separate 7 AM send task (_shared/orchestrator/run.py send, FS_MODE=send) and ONLY for rows on the night's FINAL approved send list (7_Send/ledgers/send-lists/<date>.json). --intent checks: live true, FS_MODE == live_mode (send), today >= live_from, a business day, 07:00 ET or later, and that the list is today's final approved list. The night run can never send (Chris 2026-10-31).

starter_kit._why: Email 3 attaches the starter kit (Rulebook I). Same file both machines; Zapier 'attachment' lookup pulls it fresh from these sent messages each fire (old machine configs, read 2026-10-31). Per-machine source message: machines.<OM>.starter_kit_source_message_id.

supply._README: THE SUPPLY RUN (Chris 2026-11-08): a separate nightly task at ~1 AM MT, every day, that stocks the shelf for the night run — discover → qualify → events (event-certainty check, pending Chris's ruling on the triggers) → people → rebuild → shelf summary. It never drafts, never touches Gmail, never sends. Its own session = its own 200-web-search platform budget. Timed (unlike the night run): hard stop so it is finished before the 7 AM ET send task.
supply._caps_why: one session's platform budget is 200 web searches SHARED by every helper in the session (learned 2026-11-08 first run: discovery used 133, qualify/people helpers then had none for domain lookups) — 90 for discovery leaves ~110 for qualify/people; adjust after timing logs
supply._events_step_why: runs only once Chris rules on the event-certainty trigger list (proposed 2026-11-08); until then the step is skipped and says so
supply._hard_stop_why: the send task fires 06:52 ET = 04:52 MT; the supply run must have released everything before then
supply.pointer_prompt: Mount the vault: call get_device_info; if connectedFolders is empty, call device_request_folder_access for /Users/<you>/ClaudeVault once. If it is still unreachable, stop and say so. On the device shell run:  python3 "$HOME/mnt/ClaudeVault/3.Human Skills Training/Marketing/Automations/_shared/orchestrator/run.py" supply   It prints your standing orders. Do exactly what they say, step by step, until they are complete. If it prints FAIL CLOSED, or the file is missing, stop and say so. Never do anything the orders did not print.
